title: Small bakeries lose bread to guessing how much to bake
claim: A 2025 study of small bakeries found bread waste is common there and that production-planning inefficiencies contribute significantly to it: bakers have to guess how many loaves to make. Knowing orders ahead is the direct fix for that guess.
source: Managing Global Transitions 23(3), 2025: inventory models (EOQ, newsvendor) applied to small bakeries
how_verified: Seen in web search result summaries on 14 Nov 2026; the paper itself could not be opened from the build session (host not reachable). Open the link to check before relying on it.
not_claimed: No figure on how often bakeries sell out, or on pre-orders' measured effect: none was found from a reliable source.

regulars.title: A third of artisan-bakery visitors buy bread there every week
regulars.quote: A third (33%) of UK adults who visit artisan bakeries now buy bread there at least once a week, while sourdough is nearly as popular as the traditional white loaf, new research from Marriage’s has revealed.
regulars.claim: A third of UK adults who visit artisan bakeries buy bread there at least once a week, and sourdough is nearly as popular as white bread.
regulars.source: Bakery Business, 10 Nov 2026: "New artisan bakery report", on Marriage's Millers' report Crafting the Future of Artisan Bakeries (https://flour.co.uk/artisan-bakery-report/)
regulars.how_verified: Found with one Linkup search on 14 Nov 2026; the page was opened through Linkup's fetch (the build session's proxy refuses bakerybusiness.com directly) and the quote above is copied exactly from it.
regulars.not_claimed: A UK consumer survey commissioned by a flour miller (Marriage's); sample size and method are not on the page. Nothing here about pre-orders, sell-outs or any single bakery.

why_unverified: The page was never opened (seen only in search summaries), so nothing was quoted from it. Code never shows or cites a finding without its URL, a quoted line and the date it was read.
